text:
maya: FYI nightly CI flagged a perf regression on the apples-to-apples job — tail latency on p99 jumped ~18% after the recent kernel-selector change. looks noisy but persistent.

omar: ugh. which job? link?

maya: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/apples-compare?run=1765432099  (apples-to-apples/generation/long-seq). baseline vs current.

tess: saw the alert. triaged briefly — it's correlated with kernel v2.4.6 -> v2.5 selector tweak (prefer matmul_core for fp16 at seq>2048).

sam: can we repro locally with replay harness and the same seed? i want exact command.

maya: yes. repro steps I used:
```
./harness/replay --model gptx-13b --replay-id nightly/2026-03-11 --seed 42 \
  --apples-config configs/apples_v2.json \
  --kernel-selector v2.5 --kv-warmup 1 --batch-timeout-ms 8
```
small differences if you drop `--kernel-selector` it matches baseline numbers.

lia: attaching quick profile I grabbed from the run (summary): kernel_conv_time +22%, kernel_dispatch_idle +10%, kv-cache misses up ~4%. full trace saved at s3://perf-traces/17654321/trace.pb

perf-bot: nightly-apples job 1765432099: regression detected (p99 +18%). Threshold breached: 12%. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/1765432099

omar: interesting that kv-cache misses ticked up. could selector be choosing a kernel that increases per-token memory churn so KV warmup doesn't stick?

tess: that was my suspicion. selector picks matmul_core which allocates a slightly different workspace pattern on certain kernels; that might evict earlier KV windows under our current GC heuristics.

sam: quick experiment idea: rerun replay with `--kv-warmup 3` and `--cache-policy aggressive` to see if p99 drops back. if yes, we know it's cache fragility.

maya: started a rerun: `./harness/replay --model gptx-13b --replay-id nightly/2026-03-11 --seed 42 --kernel-selector v2.5 --kv-warmup 3 --cache-policy aggressive` (job queued, CI link: https://ci.internal/runs/1765432150).

ci-bot: started run 1765432150 on dedicated-pool-7 (eta ~14m)

lia: also added a microbench: single-shot kernel latency across different seq lengths to isolate matmul_core vs matmul_fast. command I used: `./bench/kernel_latency --model gptx-13b --kernels matmul_core,matmul_fast --seq 512,2048,4096 --iter 200` results uploaded to https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/kernellat/17654321

sam: if the microbench shows a tail shift at 2048+ for matmul_core we're golden for root cause. otherwise might be batching heuristics interacting badly.

maya: update from rerun: p99 back within 3% of baseline when kv-warmup=3 and aggressive cache policy. looks like cache prewarm mitigates.

omar: OK that points to KV fragility. next steps: revert selector tweak for nightly CI until we patch GC/caching, add a CI apples-to-apples guard that reruns with `kv-warmup=3` on regression to reduce flakiness, and open a follow-up to tune GC.

lia: +1. i've opened PLAT-3421 to track GC heuristics and kernel workspace alignment. I also pushed a quick canary to the kernel selector to prefer matmul_fast for seq>=2048 while we investigate.

perf-bot: CI threshold policy suggestion: add a two-step check — on p99 breach trigger automated replay with `--kv-warmup=3` and if that pass then mark as "cache-sensitive" instead of failing the run. saves noisy alerts.

maya: agreed. can we implement that as a CI workflow change? sam can you follow up?

sam: yep i'll open CIPR-899 with the workflow patch: add a `replay-mitigation` step after alerts, plus a dashboard annotation explaining cache-sensitive regressions.

omar: one more ask — let's add the exact apples-to-apples config used in each nightly job to the run metadata (seed, kernel-selector, kv-warmup, batch-timeout-ms). makes triage way faster.

maya: good call. filed infra ticket INF-1282 to persist config blobs alongside artifacts.

tess: thanks all. i'll keep digging on kernel workspace allocator side. leaving notes in PLAT-3421. :coffee:

maya: closing loop for now. summary: regression due to selector choosing matmul_core which increases KV churn; temporary mitigation in CI + selector canary + GC follow-up. will post final triage in the ticket. :memo:
